question:
A 62-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of fatigue and weakness. Her hemoglobin A1c concentration was 13.5% 12 weeks ago. Her blood pressure is 152/92 mm Hg. Examination shows lower extremity edema. Serum studies show:
K+ 5.1 mEq/L
Phosphorus 5.0 mg/dL
Ca2+ 7.8 mg/dL
Urea nitrogen 60 mg/dL
Creatinine 2.2 mg/dL
Which of the following is the best parameter for early detection of this patient’s renal condition?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Type 2 diabetes mellitus" -> "increased risk of renal complications" -> "renal dysfunction" -> "progressive decline in kidney function" -> "early detection of renal condition" -> 70% CHAIN: "Serum creatinine" -> "commonly used marker for renal function" -> "early detection of renal condition" -> 80% CHAIN: "Serum urea nitrogen" -> "may indicate impaired kidney function" -> "early detection of renal condition" -> 70%
analysis: In this patient with type 2 diabetes mellitus and signs of kidney involvement, the best parameter for early detection of renal condition is urinary albumin. Microalbuminuria is an early sign of diabetic nephropathy, which can progress to overt proteinuria and renal failure.
